what_was_done.action: Wrap stuck-in-stage.ts's act() with buildDispatchContext + evaluatePreconditions BEFORE the action-route fetch (load-bearing niii phantom-wave-4 protection)
what_was_done.result: Modified src/lib/reconciler-rules/stuck-in-stage.ts. Added imports for buildDispatchContext + evaluatePreconditions from ../dispatch-preconditions and appendEvent + RECONCILER_ACTION_REFUSED from ../event-log. Added optional repoPath?: string field to StuckInStageRuleOptions (optional for backwards-compat with legacy unit tests; required at production via bootstrap wiring). After the existing snapshot re-read + agent:running race-abort check (lines 348-356), inserted the precondition gate (lines 379-462). The gate evaluates against context.resumeAction (pre-wlsr.14 canned action like start-wave for development) rather than the post-wlsr.14 dispatch target run-coherence-agent — necessary because Class A NO_WAVE_BEADS / PLAN_PENDING predicates only apply to start-wave / review-plan / etc., not run-coherence-agent. Universal Class A.5 BD_STATUS_DEFERRED + BD_STATUS_CLOSED + Class C OPERATOR_DECISION_PENDING + REVIEW_NEEDS_HUMAN predicates fire regardless (appliesTo returns true for every action). On refusal: structured warn-line tagged reconciler_dispatch_refused with rule/epicId/action/stage/refusalCode/failedCheck/reason fields + appendEvent of type RECONCILER_ACTION_REFUSED to opts.repoPath with ruleName=stuck-in-stage + action=resumeAction + early return without dispatching. matches() logic, the 15-min idempotency window (line ~282), and the existing stage→action lookup table all untouched per AC scope.

what_was_done.action: Handle HTTP 412 from the action route as a refusal, not an HTTP failure (architecture § Seam 5 defense-in-depth)
what_was_done.result: Modified the existing `if (!res.ok) throw` path at the rule's fetch site. New branch ahead of the throw (lines 533-571): if res.status === 412, read body, log warn-line tagged reconciler_dispatch_refused_at_route with httpStatus + body, appendEvent of type RECONCILER_ACTION_REFUSED with refusalCode='ROUTE_REFUSED_412' + failedCheck='route-side-precondition' + reason=<body>, return without throwing. Distinguishes route-side precondition refusal (race window between rule check and route check) from a genuine HTTP failure that the existing throw path handles. Mirrors ehp.4's 412 handler in marker-driven-routing.ts.

deviations_from_ac: Two clarifications: (1) The bead description text mentions evaluating the precondition gate against the dispatch action, but the rule dispatches run-coherence-agent (post-wlsr.14 cutover) while the niii phantom-wave-4 protection requires evaluating against start-wave (the resumeAction) so the Class A NO_WAVE_BEADS predicate's appliesTo returns true. I used context.resumeAction for the precondition action (with run-coherence-agent fallback) — explicitly documented inline as the stuck-in-stage-specific signal per the bead's risk flag warning ('Each rule has its own snapshot-re-read shape; do not blindly copy [ehp.4's pattern]. resumeAction is the stuck-in-stage-specific signal'). The 412 handler still uses run-coherence-agent in its event payload because that IS the action the route received. (2) The bead specifies 4 ACs but I added a 5th test (idempotency-window safety check — verifying refusal events use reconciler-action-refused not reconciler-action-taken) to surface the FOLLOW-ON gap explicitly at test-time and prevent silent regression of the matches() lastEvent-clock semantics. Pure additive test coverage; no scope expansion to the source file.
surprises_or_findings:
1. The reconciler core (reconciler.ts:381) appends `reconciler-action-taken` UNCONDITIONALLY after every act() returns (whether refused or successful) — this consumes the (rule, key) idempotency bucket even on refusals. Architecture ADR-006 calls for refusals to live in a SEPARATE bucket keyed (epicId, ruleName, refusalCode, 15-min window). Implementing the separate bucket requires a reconciler.ts change which is OUT OF SCOPE for ehp.5 per the bead's risk-flag guidance ('document the gap as FOLLOW-ON if not addressed in this bead's scope'). Mirrored from ehp.4's identical finding — this is a Wave-3-wide gap, not a per-bead issue. Documented inline in the rule's precondition-gate comment AND in this marker's recommendation_for_next.
2. Class A `plan-file-exists` predicate fires BEFORE Class A `wave-beads-exist` and `plan-not-pending` because PER_ACTION_PRECONDITIONS lists plan-file-exists first. In a tmpdir test repo (no .beads/plans/<epicId>.md), the LOAD-BEARING niii test would refuse with PLAN_FILE_MISSING instead of NO_WAVE_BEADS. Fix: created a writePlanFile() helper that writes a stub plan file. Realistic — the niii phantom-wave-4 scenario in production HAS a plan file (the epic was planned in a prior wave); the failure mode is 'no OPEN wave-4 beads', not 'no plan'. Documented in the test file's writePlanFile JSDoc.
3. listOpenWaveBeads's published return type is WaveBead[] not string[] — buildDispatchContext maps b.id internally so the test mock returns []  (empty WaveBead array). Caught early in test development; no behaviour impact.
4. Bootstrap's repoPath was already in scope (used by adjacent rules) — my edit is purely a 1-line addition to the buildStuckInStageRule options. No bootstrap signature change.
5. ARCHITECTURE.md already had references to stuck-in-stage.ts (ehp.5) in ehp.6 / ehp.8 / ehp.9 sections (sibling Wave-3/Wave-4 beads landed before ehp.5) — they cited 'mirrors the pattern established by stuck-in-stage.ts (ehp.5)'. My new section makes those references resolve.
whats_open: FOLLOW-ON (separate reconciler-core bead, mirrored from ehp.4): refusals consume the `reconciler-action-taken` idempotency bucket because reconciler.ts:381 appends that event unconditionally after act() returns. Architecture ADR-006 calls for a SEPARATE bucket keyed (epicId, ruleName, refusalCode, 15-min window). Suggested approach: have act() return a tagged result {kind: 'taken' | 'refused', refusalCode?} and have the reconciler core branch on it. Not load-bearing for the niii phantom-wave-4 protection (the rule still refuses correctly every tick — refusing again 15 min later is the same refusal), but matters for the 'transient refusal crowds out a real dispatch' edge case.
